author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka ïalum-ïalang ban ïathir ïa ka dei ka lait ruh ym ju sotan shuh.
english: Gatherings to deliberate together upon what is righteous and what is transgressive are no longer convened.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Uba im ha ka Hok, un ïoh ïa ka jingsuk bad ka jingshngaiñ ha ka shnong ka thaw.
english: He who lives in Righteousness shall obtain peace and security within the village community.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Khasi kim mane dur mane maw, hynrei ki mane ïa U Blei Uba U Nongthaw marwei.
english: The Khasis worship neither carved idols nor stones, but adore God the Supreme Creator alone.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka Mei-rad ka Kmie-tymmen ka long ka tynrai jong ka ïing ka sem bad ka kur ka jait.
english: The ancestral grandmother is the root foundation of the hearth, home, and matrilineal descent.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki tymmen ki ong ba ka ktien kaba la mih na ka shyntur kam lah shuh ban kylla dien.
english: The elders declare that the word once uttered from the mouth can never retreat backward.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jingpynjot mariang ka long ka jingbym khein burom ïa ka jingthaw U Blei.
english: The reckless destruction of nature constitutes gross disrespect toward the handiwork of God.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ki Khasi ki ju pynieng mawbynna ban kynmaw ïa ki kpa-tymmen bad ki kmie-tymmen.
english: The Khasis traditionally erect upright megalithic stones (Mawbynna) in solemn remembrance of ancestral fathers and mothers.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
section: Life Cycle: Ka Jer Ka Thoh
khasi: Haba kha ïa u khunlung, ki ju pynlong ïa ka niam jer thoh ban ai kyrteng ïa u.
english: Upon the birth of an infant child, the naming ritual (Ka Jer Ka Thoh) is performed to bestow an auspicious name.

author: U Sib Charan Roy
khasi: Ka jingïapynskhem ka long da kaba theh kiad bad duwai ha khmat U Blei bad ki sakhi.
english: The marriage pledge is solemnized by ceremonial libation and prayers offered before Almighty God and human witnesses.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U bat kawei ka kot ha la ka kti, bad kawei ka jingkit kaba khia halor ka met jong u.
english: A book in his hand, and a great heavy burden upon his back.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la ong ha ki, Ko tnga baieit bad ko khun baieit, ka jingkit kaba khia ka la ban ha nga.
english: He said unto them, O my dear wife, and you the children of my bowels, a dreadful burden presseth sore upon me.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la jubab, Ko Saheb, nga pule ha kane ka kot ba nga dei ban ïap bad ban shah bishar ha khmat U Blei.
english: He answered, Sir, I perceive by the book in my hand that I am condemned to die, and after that to come to judgment.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ong U Nongiathuhkhana, Khmih sah ïatai ka jingshai bad mareh beit beit sha ka.
english: Keep that light in your eye, and go up directly thereto: so shalt thou see the gate.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la pynïeng biang ïa u halor ka lynti kaba skhem.
english: And set him upon sound ground, and bid him go on his way.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la rwai da ka sur kaba bang, U la pynlait ïa nga na ka jingkit ka jong nga!
english: Then he gave three leaps for joy, and went out singing, Blest Cross! blest Sepulchre! blest rather be the Man that there was put to shame for me!

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Apollyon u la pyrshang ban pynduh-mynsiem ïa u bad ban phai dien ïa u sha ka Shnong Jingjot.
english: Apollyon sought to break his spirit and force him to return back to the City of Destruction.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki nongïew ki la pynsalia ïa u Pilgrim bad u Faithful namar ba ki jaiñkup jong ki ki ïapher bad kim kwah thied ïa ki tiar jong ka ïew.
english: The fair-goers made a great hubbub about them, because their apparel was so different and they set light by all their worldly wares.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Pilgrim u la kynmaw ba u don kawei ka shabi ha la ka pla kaba kyrteng Ka Kular.
english: Now, a little before day, good Christian, as one half amazed, brake out in this passionate speech: I have a key in my bosom, called Promise, that will open any lock in Doubting Castle.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Ki la ïalum ban pom noh ïa uta u dieng, hynrei manba ki la thiah miet, uta u dieng u la koit biang kumba ju long.
english: They assembled together to fell that colossal tree, but every night as they slept, the tree miraculously healed itself anew.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Hyndai la don ka jingkieng ksiar kaba pynïasoh ïa ka bneng bad ka pyrthei halor une u lum.
english: In primordial antiquity there stood a golden celestial ladder connecting heaven and earth directly upon this summit.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: U Manik Raitong u long u khunswet uba duk tam ha ka shnong, hynrei uba shemphang ha ka tem sharati.
english: Manik Raitong was the poorest orphan in the realm, yet the most sublime master of the bamboo Sharati flute.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: U Thlen u long u bsein uba khraw uba shong ha kawei ka krem kaba jylliew ha Dainthlen harud Sohra.
english: U Thlen was a monstrous mythical serpent who dwelled within a deep cavern at Dainthlen near the cliffs of Sohra.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
khasi: Ki paidbah ki la phiah bad bam ïa ka doh jong u, hynrei kawei ka tymmen ka la klet ban bam ïa la ka bynta.
english: The assembled villagers divided and ate its flesh to extinguish the curse, but an old woman forgot to consume her portion.

source_book: Ki Dienjat Jong Ki Longshwa & Kot Pule
author: Traditional Oral Lore / Babu Jeebon Roy
section: Folktale: Ka Sngi bad U Bnai
khasi: Haba u Bnai u la pyrshang ban pynsniew ïa la ka para, ka Sngi ka la theh dpei ïa ka khmat jong u.
english: When the Moon attempted to dishonour his own sister, the Sun indignantly hurled fireplace ashes straight into his face.
